items.rationale: The failed indoor heating pipe is covered under §2.4.3(a). Section 7.1.9 limits payment to plain copper: 6.4 m × €15 = €96.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow the standard copper equivalents, not the chrome premium: 4 × €10 = €40.
Section 7.1.9 limits these replacement fittings to the standard copper rate: 5 × €20 = €100.
Section 7.1.9 allows the standard copper equivalent: 1 × €20 = €20.
Minor repair fixings are covered under §7.1.7(c): 8 × €1.10 = €8.80, within the range revealed in Case 40.
The 10 mm clamps do not match the documented repair dimensions and are likely excluded under §7.1.8(e). If shown to be repair fixings, 4 × €5.50 = €22.
Repair fixings are covered under §7.1.7(c); the reference rate gives 4 × €6.20 = €24.80.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers customary repair labour. No separate upgrade labour is itemised, so the full billed quantity is priced at 6.75 hours × €88, approximately €595.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers the helper's repair labour at the reference rate: 5.75 hours × about €73, or approximately €418.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 limit re-insulation to the cost of the original rock-wool specification: 6 × €20 = €120.
Binding wire is a repair consumable under §7.1.7(c): 2 kg × €9.80 = €19.60.
Section 7.1.9 excludes the sensor because none was installed before the loss. The conditional gross estimate is €110 for one app-connected sensor.
Section 7.1.9 excludes the valve because it is a new addition, not a replacement. The conditional gross estimate is €165 for one comparable brass mixing valve.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) allow minor repair consumables billed as a lump sum: 1 × €36 = €36.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the contractor's first travel charge on this invoice: 1 × €79 = €79.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover disposal of the removed repair debris. The single charge is estimated at €60, within the €58–€61 range in Case 40.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes separately billed processing charges. The conditional estimate is €30 for one fee.
